course_summary:
ISEN 637 | Stochastic Dynamic Programming | Spring 2026
Instructor: Alfredo Garcia | alfredo.garcia@tamu.edu
Meets: TR 12:45PM - 2:00PM | ZACH 261
Grading: Homework/Exercises [40%], 1 Mid-term Exam [25%], Final Project [35%]
Topics: Ricatti Equations, Euler's Equation, Temporal Difference Learning, Regularized MDPs, Soft Q-Learning, Inverse Reinforcement Learning, LLM training, Controlling a Markov Process, Principle of Optimality, Backward Recursion, Inventory Control, Renewable Resource Exploitation, Linear Quadratic Control, Value Iteration, Policy Iteration, Q-Learning, Policy Gradients, Actor-Critic methods, Markov decision process (MDP) formulation, Bellman's equation, value function, optimal policy function, Infinite Horizon Dynamic Programming, formulate stochastic dynamic optimization problems, analyze stochastic dynamic optimization problems, identify optimal solutions, stage-wise stochastic-decision processes, finite-horizon models, infinite-horizon discounted total cost models, average cost models, finite horizon problems, infinite horizon problems, analytical tools, numerical tools, statistical techniques, stochastic dynamic optimization, deterministic dynamic optimization, discrete time, reinforcement learning methods
Prerequisites: ISEN 609 and ISEN 622, or approval of the instructor
